entry.evidence: The Geostationary Interferometric Infrared Sounder (GIIRS) onboard China's FengYun-4A geostationary satellite provides an unprecedented opportunity to observe the three-dimensional thermodynamic structure of typhoons

sequences.source_document: Feng et al. 2022, Atmospheric Research 280, 106391 (published PDF and XML text)

steps.action: Introduce the FY-4A GIIRS, the first geostationary hyperspectral infrared sounder, built and characterized by others, as the capability that opens the work.
steps.quote: FY-4A is the first geostationary weather satellite to carry the Geostationary Interferometric Infrared Sounder

steps.action: Pose the questions left open by Yin et al. (2021): GIIRS impact on more typhoon cases, the mechanism of that impact, and the unstudied assimilation of GIIRS retrieved profiles.
steps.quote: In addition, the assimilation of the vertical temperature and moisture profile retrieved from the GIIRS radiance observations has not been studied yet

steps.action: Run field campaigns of targeted observation for five live typhoons (2020-2021): sensitive regions come from CNOP and the GIIRS scanning path is adjusted to cover them.
steps.quote: the operational scanning path of the GIIRS was adaptively adjusted to observe the aforementioned sensitive regions and their surroundings

steps.action: Retrieve temperature profiles from GIIRS radiances, using regression and physical retrievals in clear sky and dual-regression in cloudy sky (algorithms of other groups).
steps.quote: Both the statistical regression retrieval algorithm and the nonlinear physical retrieval algorithm developed by Li et al. (2000) are implemented under clear sky conditions

steps.action: Preprocess the retrievals: keep quality flag 0 only, set error standard deviations of 2.0-4.0 K tuned in preliminary experiments, and superob to a 0.3° by 0.3° prism over two model layers and 30 min.
steps.quote: which is approximately optimal in our preliminary experimental evaluation

steps.action: Check the sensitivity of track forecasts to the superob horizontal box size around 30 km in a preliminary evaluation (not shown).
steps.quote: Our preliminary evaluation showed limited sensitivity of the TC track forecasts to the selection of

steps.action: Configure HWRF v3.9a on the two outer domains (18/6 km) with GSI-based EnVar on D02, non-cycling cold start from GFS/GEFS, full ensemble covariance from 20 members, and fixed localization.
steps.quote: We do not run cycling DA experiments

steps.action: Design paired data-denial experiments for each of eight cases: BASE (operational observations) and BASE+GIIRS (BASE plus superobbed GIIRS temperature profiles), verified against CMA best track, GDAS winds and CPC precipitation.
steps.quote: we designed two experiments for each Typhoon case for comparison

steps.action: Produce free forecasts of 1.25 to 4 days from both analyses for each case.
steps.quote: with an output frequency of 6 h

steps.action: Compare track forecasts with best track: BASE+GIIRS is better beyond two days in five of eight cases and similar in the Maysak and Higos cases; mean error is lower beyond 2.5 days.
steps.quote: BASE+GIIRS presents better typhoon track forecasts than BASE mainly beyond two days for five out of eight cases

steps.action: Test the mean track-error difference with a paired t-test: it is significant at the 0.05 level at 3 to 3.5 days.
steps.quote: which is statistically significant at the 0.05 level of the paired t-test.

steps.action: Propose that the case dependence (small impact for Maysak) comes from a more skillful BASE forecast and a more accurate first guess.
steps.quote: The limited DA impact of the GIIRS temperature retrieval for typhoon Maysak can be attributed to the relatively more skillful track

steps.action: Select the contrasting Chan-hom (large impact) and Maysak (small impact) cases for the mechanism diagnostics.
steps.quote: by analyzing and comparing these two cases

steps.action: Map and count the assimilated observations: operational data are sparse and far from the vortex; GIIRS data are dense (over 50,000 per case) but sparse near the vortex and at 250-400 hPa.
steps.quote: the GIIRS data from the FY-4A satellite provide a much denser observation network

steps.action: Compare the first-guess and analysis fit to the GIIRS retrievals (|O-B| against |O-A|): about 25% reduction for Chan-hom, about 10% for Maysak, and 7-27% across all cases, which supports the first-guess hypothesis.
steps.quote: a more accurate analysis field can be obtained for the temperature by assimilating the temperature retrieval from GIIRS

steps.action: Invoke steering-flow control of TC motion as the frame for the mechanism.
steps.quote: It is widely understood that the movement of TCs is dominantly governed by the steering flow.

steps.action: Compute the initial 500-hPa steering flow: BASE+GIIRS has a southward increment of about 1 m/s, consistent with its more southerly Chan-hom track.
steps.quote: which is consistent overall with the southerly shift in the TC track in BASE+GIIRS

steps.action: Diagnose the chain from temperature to height to wind through the hydrostatic relationship (correlation about -0.4 along the transect); differences are much smaller for Maysak (not shown); the steering-flow difference persists and grows in the forecast.
steps.quote: This indicates the influence of assimilating temperature observations on the GH analysis through the hydrostatic relationship.

steps.action: Verify the 2.5-day Chan-hom wind forecasts against GDAS: RMSE falls by about 10% at 500 hPa and about 33% at 1000 hPa near the coast.
steps.quote: BASE+GIIRS clearly shows a better wind forecast than BASE at mid-levels

steps.action: Extend the wind verification to all eight cases: RMSE is 1-2 m/s lower beyond 2.5 days, but the difference is not statistically significant.
steps.quote: the sample-mean wind RMSE of BASE+GIIRS and BASE are very close within the first 2.5 days

steps.action: Verify Chan-hom 24-h land precipitation against CPC gauge analysis: BASE+GIIRS overpredicts the eastern center less.
steps.quote: BASE+GIIRS presents a much smaller area with precipitation >120 mm than BASE for the eastern center

steps.action: Score precipitation for all cases with the threat score (>50 mm): five of eight cases improve and the mean TS is about 7.6% higher.
steps.quote: Five out of the eight cases show improved prediction skill of BASE+GIIRS

steps.action: Keep the claim that assimilating GIIRS temperature retrievals improves typhoon track forecasts beyond about 2.5 days, by up to 100 km on average, with case dependence.
steps.quote: the assimilation of the additional satellite retrieval generally improves the typhoon track forecasts relative to those with simply the operational observations assimilated

steps.action: Attribute the limited intensity impact to sparse near-eyewall retrievals and 16 km resolution, and point to all-sky retrievals and the higher-resolution FY-4B GIIRS.
steps.quote: The development of more accurate all-sky retrieval algorithms is crucial to enhance the utility of the GIIRS observations

end.claim: Assimilating FY-4A GIIRS temperature-profile retrievals in HWRF EnVar reduces typhoon track errors beyond about 2.5 days by up to about 100 km on average (significant at 3-3.5 days), with case dependence.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the paired BASE versus BASE+GIIRS track comparison against best track across eight cases, with its paired t-test, there would be no impact claim.

gates.evidence: Action: the GIIRS scan was steered to CNOP sensitive regions on the premise that observing them improves forecasts (p. 2), but this paper does not test that premise. Claim: the paired comparison could have shown no gain; three of eight cases showed none, and significance was tested (p. 6). Registration: the error standard deviations and superob settings were chosen in preliminary experiments (p. 2), and nothing is reported as fixed in advance.

imports.item: paired t-test for significance of track-error differences

limits: The XML text holds only the abstract and captions, so body steps are located by printed page. Results described as 'not shown': the preliminary tuning of error standard deviations, the superob sensitivity, and the Maysak mechanism fields. The analysis fit is checked only against the assimilated retrievals themselves; the authors say no independent observations were available. The mechanism is diagnosed in one case (Chan-hom), with Maysak as an unshown contrast; sub-claim status: best_explanation. The wind and precipitation improvements are 'potential', and the wind differences are not significant; sub-claim status: none/suggestive. The effectiveness of the retrieval algorithm is inferred only indirectly from forecast gains; sub-claim status: weak capability_characterized. Only eight cases are used, all from non-cycled cold-start runs, and intensity is not improved. The headline is coded confirmed against an implicit null, since no named rival exists (inference). The composition is none_fits because the walk is an observing-system (data-denial) experiment: a computer-set A/B comparison over cases found in nature, following a new capability, with the question posed before any phenomenon is established. No review file was supplied.

disagreements.target: Yin et al. (2021), direct GIIRS radiance assimilation for Typhoon Maria (2018)
disagreements.support: Yin et al. studied a single case and did not examine the mechanism; this paper tests eight cases with retrievals and diagnoses the mechanism, finding case-dependent gains.
disagreements.quote: more cases are needed to evaluate the impacts of assimilating GIIRS data on TC analyses and forecasts
